affect.sentence: Cities affect people in different ways.
affect.ety: From Latin affectare, frequentative of afficere "to do something to, act on"

beneficial.sentence: Do you agree with this idea or do you think indoor activities can be just as beneficial for children?
beneficial.ety: From Latin beneficium "benefit, favor", from bene "well" + facere "to do"

cardio.sentence: Cardio machines are near the entrance.
cardio.ety: Shortening of cardiovascular, from Greek kardia "heart"

fitness.sentence: Our fitness instructors hold exercise classes over here.

hiking.sentence: For example, do you like hiking, cycling, tennis or other types of?
hiking.ety: From hike + -ing, of unknown origin (possibly dialectal)

isolation.sentence: Some people believe that social media can help people stay connected, while others think it can lead to feelings of isolation.
isolation.ety: From French isolation, from Italian isolato, from Latin insulatus "made into an island"

adjust.sentence: Here is how to start and adjust the treadmill.
adjust.ety: From French ajuster, from a- + juste "just, exact"

adopt.sentence: Do you think that in the future more people will adopt eco-friendly travel?
adopt.ety: From Latin adoptare, from ad- "to" + optare "choose, desire"

amenities.sentence: Our amenities and services are listed on the notice boards throughout the building.

pos.zh: 便利设施;令人愉快的事物

artificial.sentence: Some people believe that artificial intelligence will greatly change the kinds of jobs available in the future.
artificial.ety: From Latin artificialis, from artificium "craftsmanship", from ars "art" + facere "to make"

assistance.sentence: If you have any questions, please seek assistance from the attendants at the help desk.
assistance.ety: From Middle French assistance, from assister "to assist", from Latin assistere "to stand by"

attendants.sentence: If you have any questions, please seek assistance from the attendants at the help desk.
attendants.ety: From French attendant, from attendre "to attend, wait for"

banging.sentence: Avoid banging or tapping on the displays and enclosures.
banging.ety: From bang + -ing; bang from Old Norse banga "to hammer"

basketball.sentence: Have they traveled to see a football game, basketball game or other types of sports?
basketball.ety: From basket + ball; coined by James Naismith in 1891

benches.sentence: There are many benches in the weightlifting area.
benches.ety: From Old English benc, from Proto-Germanic bankiz

bikes.sentence: We have plenty of exercise bikes for cardio training.
bikes.ety: Shortening of bicycle, from bi- "two" + Greek kyklos "circle, wheel"

calendar.sentence: Check out our calendar of upcoming events, many of which are family friendly.
calendar.ety: From Latin calendarium "account book", from kalendae "calends (first day of month)"

cats.sentence: Bears, wolves, and large cats are to the right.
cats.ety: From Old English catt, from Latin cattus, possibly from Afro-Asiatic

choices.sentence: I'd like to ask you some questions about career choices.
choices.ety: From Old French chois, from choisir "to choose", from Frankish kausjan

chosen.sentence: Do you think this trend will continue in your chosen field?

pos.zh: 被选中的; choose的过去分词

chosen.ety: From Old English ceosan, from Proto-Germanic keusana, from PIE *geus- "to taste, choose"

classical.sentence: Classical paintings are located on the second floor.
classical.ety: From Latin classicus "of the highest class", from classis "class, division"

commute.sentence: Imagine that you could choose to commute by car, which is faster but more expensive, or by public transportation, which is slower but less expensive.
commute.ety: From Latin commutare "to change altogether", from com- + mutare "to change"

drain.sentence: Others find that cities are overwhelming and drain them of energy.
drain.ety: From Old English drēahnian, from Proto-Germanic drauginōną

dynamic.sentence: Some people find cities dynamic and exciting.
dynamic.ety: From Greek dynamikos "powerful", from dynamis "power", from dynasthai "to be able"

eco.sentence: In recent years, there has been a trend towards eco-friendly travel where people try to minimize their environmental impact while traveling, like using public transport instead of taking a taxi.
eco.ety: From Greek oikos "house, environment", from PIE *weik- "clan, household"

elephants.sentence: You can find sea lions and elephants further down the path.
elephants.ety: From Latin elephantus, from Greek elephas (genitive elephantos), probably of African origin

elevators.sentence: The elevators are located just off the main lobby.
elevators.ety: From Latin elevare "to lift up", from e- + levare "to raise"

enclosures.sentence: Avoid banging or tapping on the displays and enclosures.
enclosures.ety: From en- + closure, from Latin claudere "to close"

enjoyable.sentence: What do you think are one or two different ways to make commuting more enjoyable?
enjoyable.ety: From enjoy + -able; enjoy from Old French enjoier "to give joy to"

equipped.sentence: All of our locker rooms are equipped with showers and towels.

pos.zh: 装备好的; equip的过去分词

equipped.ety: From French équiper, from Old French esquiper "to fit out a ship", from Old Norse skipa "to arrange"

fee.sentence: To avoid being charged a late-departure fee, be sure to check out of your room on time.
fee.ety: From Middle English fee, from Anglo-French fe, from Latin feodum "fief, feudal estate"

gym.ety: Shortening of gymnasium, from Greek gymnasion, from gymnos "naked" (ancient Greeks exercised naked)

happier.sentence: For some time now, researchers have been interested in whether green spaces, such as parks, make people who live in cities happier.
happier.ety: From happy + -er; happy from Middle English hap "chance, fortune"

healthcare.sentence: For example, do they work in healthcare, education, technology, or something else?

healthier.sentence: Do you think people today have healthier eating habits than in the past?
healthier.ety: From healthy + -er; health from Old English hælth "wholeness"

hurtful.sentence: Do you think it's helpful or hurtful to workers?
hurtful.ety: From hurt + -ful; hurt from Old French hurter "to knock, strike"

indoor.sentence: Do you agree with this idea or do you think indoor activities can be just as beneficial for children?

lions.sentence: You can find sea lions and elephants further down the path.
lions.ety: From Latin leo, from Greek leon, probably from a Semitic source

lobby.sentence: The elevators are located just off the main lobby.
lobby.ety: From Medieval Latin lobia "covered walkway", from Frankish laubja "shelter"

lounge.sentence: Our hotel lounge is available for relaxation.
lounge.ety: Of uncertain origin; perhaps from French s'allonger "to stretch out"

luggage.sentence: If needed, we can store your bags in the luggage storage room.
luggage.ety: From lug + -age; lug from Scandinavian, possibly from Old Norse lugga "to pull"

machines.sentence: Cardio machines are near the entrance.
machines.ety: From French machine, from Latin machina, from Greek mēkhanē "device, means"

maps.sentence: We have maps to help you find your way.
maps.ety: From Latin mappa "napkin, cloth" (originally cloth on which maps were drawn)

mats.sentence: We do encourage the use of yoga mats for stretching out.
mats.ety: From Old English matta, from Latin matta, from Punic or Phoenician

minimize.sentence: In recent years, there has been a trend towards eco-friendly travel where people try to minimize their environmental impact while traveling, like using public transport instead of taking a taxi.

photography.sentence: This week is your last chance to see the special exhibit on photography.

picnic.sentence: The picnic area's a perfect place to enjoy your lunch.
picnic.ety: From French pique-nique, of unknown origin, possibly from piquer "to pick" + nique "trifle"

renovation.sentence: The sculpture hall is currently under renovation.
renovation.ety: From Latin renovatio, from renovare "to renew", from re- + novus "new"

respect.sentence: While you're exploring the grounds, please respect all wildlife and follow the posted rules at all times.
respect.ety: From Latin respectus "regard, consideration", from respicere "to look back at"

restroom.sentence: Our restroom facilities are located just beside the entrance.

rules.sentence: While you're exploring the grounds, please respect all wildlife and follow the posted rules at all times.
rules.ety: From Old French riule, from Latin regula "straight stick, rule", from regere "to guide"

sculpture.sentence: The sculpture hall is currently under renovation.
sculpture.ety: From Latin sculptura, from sculpere "to carve, engrave"

services.sentence: Our amenities and services are listed on the notice boards throughout the building.
services.ety: From Latin servitium "slavery, service", from servus "slave, servant"

spaces.sentence: For some time now, researchers have been interested in whether green spaces, such as parks, make people who live in cities happier.

spontaneous.sentence: When you travel, do you prefer to plan the details of your trip in advance or do you prefer to be spontaneous and explore your destination without sticking to a plan?
spontaneous.ety: From Latin spontaneus, from sponte "of one's own accord"

stressful.sentence: Some people believe that commuting can be stressful and tiring.
stressful.ety: From stress + -ful; stress from Latin strictus "tight, drawn tight"

tapping.sentence: Avoid banging or tapping on the displays and enclosures.
tapping.ety: From tap + -ing; tap from Old French taper "to tap"

taxi.sentence: In recent years, there has been a trend towards eco-friendly travel where people try to minimize their environmental impact while traveling, like using public transport instead of taking a taxi.
taxi.ety: Shortening of taxicab, from taximeter cab, from French taximètre "taximeter"

timings.sentence: You can check the schedule for available classes and timings.
timings.ety: From time + -ing; time from Old English tima, from Proto-Germanic timon

towels.sentence: All of our locker rooms are equipped with showers and towels.
towels.ety: From Old French toaille, from Frankish thwahlja, from Proto-Germanic thwahlijan

treadmill.sentence: Here is how to start and adjust the treadmill.
treadmill.ety: From tread + mill, originally a device for grinding by treading

usage.sentence: Finally, do you think social media use will continue to grow in the future, or will people start to limit their usage?
usage.ety: From Old French usage, from Latin usus "use, custom", from uti "to use"

weightlifting.sentence: There are many benches in the weightlifting area.

wipes.sentence: Please use the wipes provided at each station for cleaning equipment after use.
wipes.ety: From Old English wipian, from Proto-Germanic wipōną "to wipe"

wolves.sentence: Bears, wolves, and large cats are to the right.
wolves.ety: From Old English wulf, from Proto-Germanic wulfaz, from PIE *wĺ̥kʷos

yoga.sentence: We do encourage the use of yoga mats for stretching out.
yoga.ety: From Sanskrit yoga "union, yoking", from yuj "to yoke, unite"
